_meta.indication: For the treatment of adult patients who have relapsed or refractory AML with a FMS-like tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3) mutation as detected by an FDA-approved test.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, open-label study comparing gilteritinib 120 mg daily versus salvage chemotherapy (randomized 2:1); the NDA determination relied on a prespecified interim single-arm analysis of CR/CRh in the gilteritinib arm.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with relapsed or refractory AML with a FLT3 mutation as detected by an FDA-approved test; the FDA Efficacy Analysis Population had median age 60 years, 46% male, 60% white.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Rate of complete remission (CR)/complete remission with partial hematologic recovery (CRh)
pivotal_trials.result: CR/CRh rate 21.0% (29/138; 95% CI: 14.5, 28.8); CR 11.6% (16/138), CRh 9.4% (13/138); median duration of CR/CRh 4.6 months.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) were myalgia/arthralgia, transaminase increase, fatigue/malaise, fever, noninfectious diarrhea, dyspnea, edema, rash, pneumonia, nausea, stomatitis, cough, headache, hypotension, dizziness and vomiting. Potentially life-threatening/serious risks included QT prolongation (1.4% had QTcF >500 msec), differentiation syndrome, and pancreatitis.
target_moa: Gilteritinib is a kinase inhibitor that inhibits FMS-like tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3), decreasing FLT3 receptor signaling (phosphorylation of STAT5, AKT, and ERK); it also inhibits AXL, LTK, ALK, and KIT.
companion_dx_detail: LeukoStrat CDx FLT3 Mutation Assay, which detects FLT3 ITD, D835, or I836 mutations to select patients for treatment.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee.

description.text: Added boxed warning for differentiation syndrome and related labeling updates based on final analysis of Study 2215-CL-0301

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the following updates to the United States Prescribing Information: addition of a boxed warning for differentiation syndrome; addition of dosage modifications for XOSPATA-related toxicities (Section 2.3); addition of differentiation syndrome in warnings and precautions (Section 5.1), revisions to the warnings and precautions for posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome, prolonged QT interval and pancreatitis (Sections 5.2, 5.3, 5.4); updates in adverse reactions (Section 6.1); updates based on the final analysis of Study 2215-CL-0301 (Section 14), and addition of patient counseling information about differentiation syndrome (Section 17). Also, the Patient Package Insert was converted to a Medication Guide.

orphan_indication.text: Gilteritinib has orphan designation for the treatment of AML, and is therefore exempt from PREA pediatric assessment requirements.

citations.quote: Because this drug product for this indication has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.

summary.text: NDA 211349 was submitted as an Original Type 1 NDA and received Priority review; the drug had orphan drug designation for AML. Although the sponsor requested accelerated approval, the review team recommended and FDA granted regular (traditional) approval under 21 CFR 314.105 based on durable CR/CRh and conversion to transfusion independence in the ADMIRAL trial.

requirement.text: PMR 3542-1: Demonstrate safety of long-term treatment with gilteritinib via an integrated report summarizing safety outcomes when all patients on 2215-CL-0101, 2215-CL-0102 and 2215-CL-0301 have completed at least three years of treatment.

citations.quote: PMR 3542-1 Demonstrate safety of long-term treatment with gilteritinib. Submit an integrated report and the supporting data files to summarize the safety outcomes when all patients on 2215-CL-0101, 2215-CL-0102 and 2215-CL-0301 have completed at least three years of treatment with gilteritinib or withdrew earlier.

requirement.text: PMR 3542-2: Characterize the risk of differentiation syndrome via a pooled analysis of incidence, signs/symptoms, duration, and response to intervention in AML patients with a FLT3 mutation.

citations.quote: PMR 3542-2 Characterize the risk of differentiation syndrome in patients receiving gilteritinib for treatment of acute myeloid leukemia with a FLT3 mutation. Conduct a pooled analysis to characterize gilteritinib-related differentiation syndrome, specifically incidence, observed signs and symptoms, duration, and response to intervention based on patient-level data from on-going trials in patients with acute myeloid leukemia. Submit the study report and analysis data set.

requirement.text: PMR 3542-3: Provide data establishing that the risks are outweighed by benefit for patients with a FLT3 tyrosine kinase domain (TKD) mutation, with outcomes for at least 30 FLT3-TKD patients.

citations.quote: PMR 3542-3 Provide data to establish that the risks of gilteritinib are outweighed by the potential benefit for patients with AML having a mutation in the FLT3 tyrosine kinase domain (TKD). Submit a summary report and a supporting data set that includes outcomes for at least 30 patients with a FLT3-TKD mutation.

requirement.text: PMC 3542-4: Clarify the sensitivity of various FLT3 mutations other than ITDs and the D835Y TKD mutation by in vitro testing, including 1836 mutations, other D835 mutations, and other AML-reported mutations.

citations.quote: PMC 3542-4 Clarify the sensitivity of various FLT3 mutations other than internal tandem duplications (ITDs) and the D835Y tyrosine kinase domain mutation by in vitro testing. Include testing of 1836 mutations, other D835 mutations, and other mutations reported to occur in AML. Submit a summary report.
